claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
A 500–700 °C substrate preheat can be implemented during laser-based additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi.
AlCrFeNiSi can be processed by a standard laser-based AM method in an inert atmosphere using typical alloy-specific laser parameters.
Substrate preheating reduces the temperature differential between the melt pool and surrounding material.
Reducing the melt-pool temperature differential diminishes thermal shock.
Substrate preheating enhances in situ diffusion and accelerates homogenization of the alloying elements.
Moderated temperature gradients and enhanced diffusion produce a more compositionally uniform microstructure.
Substrate preheating produces a refined microstructure.
Substrate preheating reduces residual stress in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating reduces processing defects such as cracks and porosity in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defect formation improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Relative to ambient-substrate AM controls, preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will have higher yield strength.
Relative to ambient-substrate AM controls, preheated AlCrFeNiSi samples will have greater toughness.
Conventionally additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi made on an ambient-temperature substrate is known to exhibit notable compositional segregation.
Conventionally additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi made on an ambient-temperature substrate is known to exhibit high residual stress and defect formation.
SEM/EDS mapping can be used to assess microstructural homogeneity and elemental segregation in laser-additively manufactured material.
The intervention is limited to part sizes for which substrate preheating can be maintained uniformly.
The proposed benefit depends on the preheat temperature not causing oxidation or excessive grain growth.
